somnath-temple: The first of the twelve Jyotirlingas, on Gujarat's Arabian Sea coast — rebuilt several times after historic raids, its current shikhara dates to 1951.
mallikarjuna-temple: A hilltop Jyotirlinga above the Krishna river gorge at Srisailam, one of the few shrines counted among both the Jyotirlingas and the Shakti Peethas.
mahakaleshwar-temple: Ujjain's Jyotirlinga, unusual for facing south, known for its pre-dawn Bhasma Aarti where the deity is ritually bathed in sacred ash.
omkareshwar-temple: A Jyotirlinga on a Narmada river island shaped like the sacred Om symbol, reached by a footbridge from the mainland ghats.
kedarnath-temple: A stone Shiva temple at 3,583m in the Garhwal Himalaya, reachable only on foot or by helicopter, open to pilgrims a few months each year.
bhimashankar-temple: A Jyotirlinga tucked into a forested wildlife sanctuary in the Sahyadri hills, and the source of the Bhima river.
kashi-vishwanath-temple: Varanasi's Jyotirlinga on the Ganga's ghats, rebuilt in its present form in 1780 and now linked to the river by a broad new corridor.
trimbakeshwar-temple: A black-stone Jyotirlinga near Nashik where the Godavari river is believed to originate, its inner sanctum holding three small lingas for the Trimurti.
baidyanath-temple: A Jyotirlinga at Deoghar also revered as one of the Shakti Peethas, drawing pilgrims who carry Ganga water on foot from Sultanganj.
nageshwar-jyotirlinga: A Jyotirlinga near Dwarka marked by a giant Shiva statue, one of three shrines across India that claim the name Nageshwar.
rameswaram: A Jyotirlinga and Char Dham site on an island linked to the Ramayana, famed for a pillared corridor among the longest of any Hindu temple.
grishneshwar-temple: The last of the twelve Jyotirlingas, rebuilt in the 18th century barely a kilometre from the Ellora Caves.
badrinath-temple: The Himalayan Char Dham dedicated to Vishnu, open only from spring to autumn before Garhwal's snows close the valley.
dwarkadhish-temple: Krishna's Char Dham temple in his legendary capital of Dwarka, its five-storey spire visible from far along the Gujarat coast.
jagannath-temple-puri: The Char Dham temple on Odisha's coast, famous for its annual Rath Yatra, when the deities are pulled through the streets on giant wooden chariots.
